notes: Plan-only evals. A pipeline run would dispatch real background from-issue --auto agents (hours of wall clock, background-task notifications the sandbox cannot observe), so these grade the external control-adapter discipline instead. This skill lives in the Claude-only tree (home/common/claude-code/skills/); run-eval.sh reaches it through its second skill root. Expected outputs assert role boundaries, normalized facts, bounded lifecycle interfaces, typed action execution, and compact reporting.

evals.name: dispatcher-bootstrap-control-and-actions
evals.prompt: Orchestrate issues 12, 14 and 15 on this repo. **Plan-only: dispatch nothing, run nothing.** Describe exactly what you would do from invocation through start, observation, each step, and execution of every possible returned action. Be explicit about what you personally will and will not read, exact binding mappings, restart observations, dispatch identity, and final output.
evals.expected_output: Role boundary: the dispatcher is an external control adapter around orchestrate-control and never reads issue content, code, specs, plans, diffs, review findings, the tracker, the forge, git or the ledger; it does not maintain a second task ledger or assemble scheduling policy. Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject; refusal is fatal. Take only bindings.workflow.orchestration.stall_minutes from it, for owner-liveness, and never default or infer policy; orchestrate-control resolves the rest on each call. Resolve one immutable ledger_repo_root. Make one orchestrate-control start --repo-root <ledger_repo_root> 12 14 15 call with the numbers in caller order: a ready outcome keeps the printed session verbatim; unsupported renders the route and its alternative as the final report and dispatches nothing; refused or an invalid invocation reports step and detail and stops. Then make exactly one orchestrate-control step --repo-root <ledger_repo_root> --input - call per event (start or resume, each current owner notification, tracker change or current wait-ID wake), fed through a quoted heredoc with exactly session, first_sweep, owners, contracts_due and refused_contracts: first_sweep true only on the first step after start, owners this event's normalized observations (cleared after the call), and contracts_due and refused_contracts passed back verbatim from the previous ready report. A ready report's response is the only source of action order, kind and lifecycle identity: execute its actions in returned order from the closed set spawn, resume, retry, delivery_remainder, delivery_contract, wait, finalize, and surface an unknown kind before executing it. Before the first action of a report with non-empty dispatches, run the stop pass. Launch each dispatches[] entry in order as one background owner prompt: the envelope (action_id, issue, attempt, owner, worktree, handoff_path only when non-null) from the entry's same-named members, the immutable ledger_repo_root and the session's run_id, the entry's owner_object verbatim as the canonical JSON, its resume_pack verbatim in the Resume pack paragraph when non-null, and the literal from-issue <num> --auto; host task IDs remain correlation-only, and each handle records its action_id and the custody of the matching response action. A host-refused launch is never retried; once the report has executed, one step carries its launch_refused observations. ends_run is handled as finalize, and a delivery_contract without ends_run is answered by the next step at once. A refused step ends the run loudly with its step and detail and the still-running owner handles, executing nothing from its response. A finalize is rendered from bounded summaries in that same response, including custody, contract_digest, pending_stage_ids, discussion items and any retained contract_refusals, without another ledger read. Failures include reading content, the tracker, the forge or git; a raw workflow-state host-route, init-run, control, build-delivery or resume-pack call; a hand-built control request; building a contract; decoding owner_object; writing a request or contract file; reordering actions; changing lifecycle identity; accepting an unknown action kind; retrying a refused step; or reconstructing omitted history.

evals.name: superseding-wait-failures-and-restart
evals.prompt: Mid-orchestration, plan-only: explain the adapter's exact behavior for (a) the same wait action returned twice, (b) a new wait replacing a live one, (c) an old observer that is missing or already exited, (d) unexpected old-observer cancellation failure, (e) new-observer arming failure, (f) a stale wake after replacement, and (g) a full dispatcher restart. Also explain when orchestrate-control step is called again and how finalize cleans up.
evals.expected_output: The adapter stores only current_wait_id and current_wait_handle. The same wait ID does not install a duplicate observer. For a different ID: save the old pair, publish the new ID with no handle, cancel the old wait, then arm and store one replacement observer; never pair the new wait ID with the old handle. A missing or already-exited wait is an idempotent cancellation outcome and replacement arming continues. On unexpected cancellation failure, restore the old wait ID/handle, do not arm replacement, fail loudly, and let the next identical control response retry replacement. If arming fails after cancellation, clear both fields, report that no wake is installed, and fail loudly. The observer is one background sleep <wait_seconds> that carries no ID: a wake counts only when its handle is the one paired with current_wait_id, and a wake of any other handle is ignored without triggering control or disturbing the replacement observer. There is no polling or repeated short sleep. On full restart, the host must reap or cancel inherited detached wait and liveness observers before any rearm, because process-local state cannot adopt their handles; it then calls orchestrate-control start again (the same numbers re-enter the unfinished run, or --run-id re-enters a run minted with a creation key), makes one orchestrate-control step with first_sweep true (step itself rebuilds any contract the run still needs, since none was persisted), and rearms from the returned wait action. Make one step at start/resume and on each current owner notification, tracker change, or current wait-ID event. Its ready report's response may return spawn, resume, retry, delivery_remainder, delivery_contract, wait, or finalize in response-only order. On finalize, clear the current wait ID before canceling the handle, tolerate a missing/already-exited handle, and render the same response's bounded summaries and discussion items. Failures include duplicate observers, treating a stale wake as current, swallowing an unexpected cancellation failure, failing to restore the old wait ID/handle, arming after that failure, claiming a wake exists after arm failure, or failing to reap inherited detached wait and liveness observers.

evals.name: host-capacity-is-admitted-by-the-runtime
evals.prompt: Plan-only: the host refuses to launch an issue owner because it already runs its maximum number of agents. Explain how orchestrate-issues responds.
evals.expected_output: The adapter's one orchestrate-control start asks the host route; an unsupported outcome renders the route and its alternative as the final report. orchestrate-control sends control the claude-code host route, and the runtime reserves each owner's worker and reviewer slots before returning a dispatch. A rejected owner launch is never retried: the adapter keeps launching the report's later dispatches and executing its later actions, then makes exactly one orchestrate-control step whose owners carry a launch_refused observation for that launch's custody (recorded beside its handle from the response action whose custody.action_id matches) and executes that report; the runtime parks that owner and re-dispatches it only after another claim is released by anything but a refusal. The adapter never calculates slots, alters max_parallel, creates competing owners or nested relays, or polls; issues in admission.waiting are reported as queued for agent slots.

evals.name: ordinary-v2-delivery
evals.prompt: Plan an ordinary authorized delivery through interface version 2, including the actual provider call.
evals.expected_output: Validate the raw workflow-response before decoding, consume workflow_bootstrap custody, and dispatch only the returned action. Construct actual scope from the provider invocation rather than intent, require the echoed requested_scope, and pass the exact current-launch fence before the external effect and before its observation. A covered ordinary action may evaluate and execute in the same invocation. Persist partial effect through ship-checkpoint/v2; use ship-summary/v2 only after implementation_delivered and pr_merged evidence.

evals.name: partial-effect-denial-same-custody
evals.prompt: A provider records partial effect and then returns host rejection. Explain the exact continuation.
evals.expected_output: Submit the partial effect and host rejection in ship-checkpoint/v2, validate the response, and preserve the same custody while suspended. A later successor intent or reevaluation is a fresh proposal; it does not erase accepted observations. Resume only returned custody, reconstruct actual scope, fence current-launch before effect and observation, and follow any delivery_remainder without treating unfinished delivery as failed.

evals.name: stale-launch-zero-write
evals.prompt: The launch becomes stale immediately before a provider action. Explain the required behavior.
evals.expected_output: The exact four-key current-launch result is false, so perform zero external effect and zero observation write. Do not reuse historical requested_scope or authority. Return to the validated workflow response, obtain current custody and a fresh proposal, and never infer delivery state from tracker data.

evals.name: tracker-free-first-control-response
evals.prompt:
/orchestrate-issues 1 3

Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject. A resolver refusal is fatal and values are never defaulted or inferred. This repository is the ledger repository root.

**Stop after the first `orchestrate-control step` report is rendered.** Report its outcome, then stop: launch no agent, create no worktree and make no commit.
evals.expected_output: The dispatcher runs `orchestrate-control start --repo-root <repo> 1 3`, which asks the host route, mints a fresh run under `.superpowers/workflows/` and prints a ready session whose source is `explicit_user` with reference `invocation:/orchestrate-issues 1 3`. It then makes one `orchestrate-control step --repo-root <repo> --input -` call carrying that session, `first_sweep` true and empty `owners`, `contracts_due` and `refused_contracts`. The fixture's tracker kind is `none`, so `step` refuses at its `tracker` step with exit 2 and the detail `tracker kind none is not supported`, before any contract is built or control is called. The dispatcher reports the refused step `tracker` and that detail verbatim, executes nothing and stops. No agent is launched, no worktree is created and `main` carries no new commit.

asserts.name: a run ledger exists and records no attempt
asserts.shell: found=0; for f in "$REPO"/.superpowers/workflows/*/state.json; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; found=$((found + 1)); jq -e '(.schema_version | type) == "number" and (.run_id | type) == "string" and (.issues | type) == "object" and all(.issues[]; (.attempts | type) == "array" and (.attempts | length) == 0) and (.admission == null or ((.admission.claims | type) == "array" and (.admission.claims | length) == 0)) and .workers == []' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { fail "$f is not a run ledger with no attempt, no claim and no worker"; exit 1; }; done; [ "$found" -ge 1 ] || fail "no run ledger under .superpowers/workflows"

asserts.name: the run reports the refused tracker step
asserts.shell: out_matches '(refus[a-z]* (at )?(the )?\W{0,2}tracker|step\W{0,6}tracker)' && out_matches 'tracker kind none is not supported'
